newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Constanta city plans up to $150 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Romania Constanta city plans up to $150 mln bonds.

text.p: The city hall of Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta plans to raise up to $150 million in municipal bonds in the first part of 1997, an official of local security firm SIRA Invest SA said on Thursday.
Constanta's mayor has signed the agreement with a consortium linking the U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers and SIRA Invest which will be the managers of the issue, the official said.
The planned issue -- up to $50 million in a private placement and a public issue of about $100 million Eurobonds -- is aimed at local and foreign investors, the official said.

He said the consortium also plans a similar arrangement with the town of Brasov, north of Bucharest. He said local authorities in the Transylvanian town had recently approved the plan to issue municipal bonds.
Romania's capital Bucharest said in August it planned to raise about $200 million in municipal bonds through Merrill Lynch International to upgrade infrastructure.

Merrill Lynch has already handled two medium-term issues on capital markets for Romania's National Bank -- a $50 million private placement last November and $225 million worth of three-year Eurobonds in June.

The municipality of Sinaia ski resort, in the southern Carpathians north-west of Bucharest, also announced it would launch a domestic bond issue worth 200 billion lei ($60 million) in the last quarter of 1996.

Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies in March. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus score, somewhat higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standard and Poor's and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
